locked_interpretation.reason: One seed passes every late-stationarity gate, while the other has inadequate effective sample size and a 95-percent stationary-null drift envelope wider than one percent. The second seed does not reject stationarity at the complete horizon, so the result is not evidence for common continued secular evolution.

scientific_findings: Every extension block has exact electron and ion source-loss accounting, excluding a detected population-ledger defect as the cause of density motion.
Integral-normalized profile-shape motion passes for both seeds, while density amplitude exhibits slow autocorrelation; the unresolved mode is predominantly global amplitude rather than spatial shape.
Mean ion current remains close to Turner Table III for both seeds, at 0.21818 and 0.21772 A/m2 versus 0.219 A/m2.
Longer histories reduce apparent secular drift, but seed-dependent correlation leaves the one-percent density-amplitude claim underpowered.

The evidence does not justify a Turner Case 1 validation claim, but it narrows the credibility problem to stochastic or feedback-driven amplitude uncertainty rather than gross conservation or profile instability.

next_stage.objective: Determine whether the slow density-amplitude variance and correlation time decrease with macro-particle count as finite-particle noise predicts, or persist as a physical/numerical feedback mode.
next_stage.required_discrimination: Compare fixed-horizon late-window amplitude variance, AR1 correlation, effective blocks, normalized shape, balance, and Turner observables at the current particle weight and at one or more lower-weight higher-particle-count levels using fresh seeds.
next_stage.decision_boundary: Only after the scaling law and equilibration horizon are characterized should a new independent-seed Turner confirmation protocol be preregistered.

claim_boundary: This is a prospective design-stage mechanism diagnosis. The prior held-out confirmation failure remains immutable; no formal Turner validation or profile pooling is authorized.
